notes:
Read-along now follows the page — and actually finds the speech balloons.

Three fixes to reading comics aloud, found from watching it run on a real webtoon chapter.

IT WASN'T FINDING ANY SPEECH BALLOONS. On a vertical webtoon the app was failing to spot a single balloon in a whole chapter, so everything was read as narration — which is also why the NARRATOR and CAST settings sounded identical, since CAST had nothing to tell apart. The page was being shrunk to a sliver before it was examined: a webtoon strip is very tall and very narrow, and the shrinking rule cared about its height, leaving it about seventy pixels wide. Balloons had nowhere to be seen. Fixed.

IT NOW FOLLOWS WHAT YOU'RE LOOKING AT. A webtoon chapter is one enormous strip holding a dozen panels, and only a fraction of it is on screen. The voice used to read the whole strip from top to bottom while the page stayed where you left it, so it was rarely talking about the picture in front of you. Each line now knows where it lives on the page, and the page scrolls to it as it is read.

IT STOPPED READING THE SCANLATION CREDITS. The credits card at the top of a chapter was being read out as though it were dialogue — including the crew names on their own. The whole card is now recognised and skipped.

Still rough, and worth saying plainly: on some titles the text itself comes out garbled — stylised lettering over colourful artwork is genuinely hard to read, and the app sometimes reads the outline of a word and its filling as two different words. Filtering that out would risk deleting real dialogue, so the proper fix is to find each balloon first and read only inside it. That is the next piece of work.
